```{r setup, include=FALSE}
# Report structure
#   R/helpers.R              all settings (thresholds, colours, tab order) and functions
#   css/lake_components.css  styles for trend badges, dashboard and guideline cards
#
# TODO (from call with Mike -- please confirm status):
#   [x] Add middle point to sample depth plot to show the three samples
#   [ ] Remove lake bottom (not sure this was done)
#   [x] Add WQ parameter guideline
#   [x] Add WQ trend statement (trend badges / dashboard)

knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
source("helpers.R")   # also loads the packages used by the report
```

```{r LoadData, include=FALSE}
# 1. Download the lake's data and optionally save a copy
site_data <- load_lake_data(params$ems_id, params$from_date)

if (params$save_csv) {
  write.csv(site_data, paste0(params$ems_id, "_data_", Sys.Date(), ".csv"), row.names = FALSE)
}

# 2. Keep only the parameters listed in the parameter CSV, drop sparse ones,
#    and put results in readable units
parameter_list <- load_parameter_list(params$parameter_file)
lake_data      <- prepare_lake_data(site_data, parameter_list)

# 3. Trend results for every parameter x depth x season (used by plots and dashboard)
trends <- calc_all_trends(lake_data)

report_date <- Sys.Date()
site_name   <- unique(lake_data$MONITORING_LOCATION)
```

---

[`r params$title` (`r unique(lake_data$EMS_ID)`)](https://governmentofbc.maps.arcgis.com/apps/MapSeries/index.html?appid=a5ffb1bcffad4407b387292f2e55899f) is located at `r site_name`. Report generated: `r format(report_date, "%B %d, %Y")`.

The plot below shows the sampling history at this site. Composite samples are indicated by a vertical line connecting the uppermost and lowermost sampling depths. Triangles (▲) indicate epilimnion (upper layer) samples; solid circles (●) indicate hypolimnion (bottom layer) samples. For lakes less than 10 m deep, a single sample 1 m below the surface represents the epilimnion and one 1 m off the bottom represents the hypolimnion.

To read more about the B.C. Lakes Monitoring Network (BCLMN) go [here](https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content?id=2493EFF1E42747E1904540DA4D2CF9DD).

```{r SampleOverviewPlot, fig.width=9, fig.height=4.5, fig.align='center', out.width="85%", dpi=120, fig.cap="Sampling dates and depth ranges"}
make_sampling_plot(lake_data)
```

<p style="font-size:0.85em; color:#666; margin-top:8px;">
n/a = fewer than 3 samples (or none) in that depth/season group.
&#8212; no trend = no statistically significant trend, or more than 50% of results were non-detects.
Badge colors indicate the <em>direction</em> of a detected trend only, not whether that direction is good or bad for water quality.

### Monitoring Results and Trends {.tabset}

Each observation is shown as a black dot in the scatter plots below. Where a statistically significant trend is detected (p < 0.05 with at least 50% of observations above the detection limit), a trend line with 95% confidence bands is displayed and a coloured trend badge is shown on the plot giving the direction and magnitude of the trend. Open orange triangles (▽) indicate non-detects and are plotted at the detection limit.

If a simple water quality guideline (that is one independent of other parameters) applies and measurements are within that guideline a green check box will display showing the guideline value, conversely if a guideline has been exceeded a yellow warning box will be displayed.

Raw data: [EnMoDS Data Search and Download](https://enmodswr.nrs.gov.bc.ca/) | [Water Quality Guidelines](https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content?id=044DD64C7E24415D83D07430964113C9)

```{r CategoryTabs, results='asis', fig.height=7, fig.width=9}
# One tab per category (order set by CATEGORIES in helpers.R), with one
# sub-tab per parameter inside it.
for (category in CATEGORIES) {
  cat("\n\n#### **", category, "** {.tabset .tabset-fade .tabset-pills}\n\n", sep = "")

  category_data <- filter(lake_data, Category == category)

  for (param in order_parameters(category_data$PARAMETER, category)) {
    render_parameter_tab(
      category_data, param, parameter_list, trends,
      report_title = params$title,
      epi_only     = param %in% EPI_ONLY_PARAMETERS
    )
  }
}
```
